record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.context_brief: Secret key distillation from all entangled states
record.original_question: Can every bipartite entangled state be used to generate secret keys, including bound entangled states for which secret key extraction need not proceed by first distilling pure singlets?

evidence.quote: Can all bipartite entangled states be used to generate secrete keys?

In [HHHO02] it is shown that some bound entangled states do allow the extraction of a secret key. This is an extreme counterexample to the idea that secret key is best generated from an entangled state by first distilling pure singlets, and using these to get the key.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\rho_{AB}$ be a bipartite quantum state on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$. The state $\rho_{AB}$ is called entangled if it cannot be written as a convex combination $\sum_i p_i \sigma^A_i \otimes \tau^B_i$ of product states. The distillable secret key rate $K_D(\rho_{AB})$ is defined as the largest rate $R \geq 0$ such that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $n_0$ with the following property: for all $n \geq n_0$ there is an LOCC (local operations and classical communication) protocol acting on $\rho_{AB}^{\otimes n}$ that outputs a classical-classical-quantum state on registers $K_A K_B E$ (with $E$ held by an eavesdropper purifying the protocol) which is $\varepsilon$-close in trace distance to an ideal secret key state $\frac{1}{2^{\lfloor nR \rfloor}} \sum_{k} |kk\rangle\langle kk|_{K_A K_B} \otimes \sigma_E$ for some $\sigma_E$.

Some bound entangled states (entangled states from which no pure maximally entangled pairs can be distilled by LOCC) are known to have $K_D > 0$, so secret key extraction need not proceed via prior distillation of singlets.

Question: Is it true that $K_D(\rho_{AB}) > 0$ for every entangled bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem (Problem 24, "Secret key from all entangled states") on the Open Quantum Problems database maintained by IQOQI. While partial progress exists — e.g., specific bound entangled states are known to yield positive distillable key, and efficiently computable upper bounds on one-way distillable key have been developed — no general proof or counterexample establishing whether every bipartite entangled state has positive distillable secret key rate is known.

status_evidence.title: Secret key from all entangled states – Open Quantum Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists partial results (bound entangled states with positive key rate, one-way distillation protocols, etc.) but no resolution of whether all entangled bipartite states yield secret key.
status_evidence.claim: Problem catalogued as an open problem with only partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Bipartite bound entanglement (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses bound entangled states with positive distillable key rate and the still-unresolved general question.
status_evidence.claim: Recent survey treats the question as still open with partial results.

status_evidence.title: Extendibility limits quantum-secured communication and key distillation
status_evidence.snippet: Provides efficiently computable upper bounds on one-way distillable key, contributing partial progress.
status_evidence.claim: Recent upper-bound work indicates the problem is still under active investigation.
